title: "Do not sort" setting in task manager sorts some task items
line: With "Do not sort", tasks keep their order after switching virtual desktops, even when one of them demands attention.
explanation: With sorting disabled, the task manager orders tasks by their row in the grouping proxy model. When switching desktops, windows from the other desktop are filtered out and back in, and the grouping proxy always appended re-inserted rows at the end, while a task demanding attention stays visible on every desktop and so keeps its place. That task therefore jumped to the front and the others came back in a different order. The grouping proxy now inserts each new ungrouped row at the position matching its source row, so the original order is kept.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: keep source order when rows are inserted ungrouped

Rows coming back from the filter, such as windows shown again after a
desktop switch, were always appended, so with sorting disabled they ended
up after any task that stayed visible. Insert them at their source position.

BUG: 444834

media.caption: Do not sort, middle XTerm demands attention: desktop 1, desktop 2, back on desktop 1. The XTerm jumps to the front and Konsole goes last.
Same steps with the fix: back on desktop 1 the order is still Konsole, XTerm, Colors.

review.text: Clean root-cause fix in `TaskGroupingProxyModel::Private::sourceRowsInserted()`. Inserting newly re-added ungrouped rows before the first `rowMap` entry whose `constFirst()` exceeds the source row preserves original order across virtual desktop switches under 'Do not sort' even when a demanding-attention window stays visible. Using `std::find_if` is safe even if `rowMap` is non-monotonic after `breakGroupFor()`, existing `QList<int> *` pointers remain valid for child `internalPointer`s, and the before/after screenshots clearly prove the fix.

reviews.text: Clean root-cause fix in `TaskGroupingProxyModel::Private::sourceRowsInserted()`. Inserting newly re-added ungrouped rows before the first `rowMap` entry whose `constFirst()` exceeds the source row preserves original order across virtual desktop switches under 'Do not sort' even when a demanding-attention window stays visible. Using `std::find_if` is safe even if `rowMap` is non-monotonic after `breakGroupFor()`, existing `QList<int> *` pointers remain valid for child `internalPointer`s, and the before/after screenshots clearly prove the fix.

The diagnosis is right. With SortDisabled, TasksModel orders by the grouping proxy's row, and TaskGroupingProxyModel::sourceRowsInserted() appended rows that the desktop filter brought back, so a demands-attention task that was never filtered out ended up first. Inserting at the first rowMap entry whose source row is greater (after adjustMap) restores source order. The change is small and in the right layer, new windows still go last, and other sort modes only see their row() tie-break become stable. The before/after strips and the regression notes (grouping by program, repeated switches) match the patch and commit message. The reporter's side wish for an option to turn off attention highlighting is a separate feature request. Nit: a tasksmodeltest/grouping-proxy case for filtered-out-and-back rows would help a maintainer, and the other append sites (rebuildMap, breakGroupFor) are untouched but don't affect this scenario.
